sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Mason County, KY?
sections.html:
In Mason County the work is divided among three Maysville offices. The PVA values property, the sheriff collects, and the County Clerk records deeds and receives prior-year delinquent bills.

  • The Property Valuation Administrator is at 220 1/2 Sutton Street, phone (606) 564-3700, open Monday to Friday 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM. The office handles assessments, mailing and property address changes, and homestead and disability exemptions.
  • The Sheriff's Office is at 120 West Third Street in the old Health Department building, phone 606-564-3309, open weekdays 9:00 am to 4:30 pm. It also has a drop box for check payments only.
  • The County Clerk is at 27 West 3rd Street, PO Box 234, phone (606) 564-3341. Hours are weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed for lunch from 11:30 to 12:30.

The PVA's page makes a point that is useful when arguing about a bill: the PVA does not set tax rates. Rates come from the fiscal court, city officials, school boards and other taxing authorities, and the sheriff collects the current year's bills.

sections.h2: What should someone selling in Mason County know about the area?
sections.html:
Mason County is a small Ohio River county in northeastern Kentucky. It was created in 1788 from Bourbon County, Virginia, and is named for George Mason, and the Ohio River forms its northern border with Brown and Adams counties in Ohio. It covers 246 square miles, 240 of them land, and adjoins Lewis, Fleming, Robertson and Bracken counties.

Maysville is the seat and largest city. Dover, Germantown and Sardis are also incorporated, and Mays Lick is a census-designated place. Other communities include Helena, Lewisburg, Minerva, Old Washington, Orangeburg and Shannon. The Census Bureau groups the county as the Maysville micropolitan area, which belongs to the Cincinnati-Wilmington-Maysville combined statistical area.

Mason County Schools runs the public system, including Mason County High School, Mason County Middle School, Mason County Intermediate School and Straub Elementary School. Population has drifted down from 17,490 in 2010 to 17,120 in 2020 and an estimated 16,936 in 2025, a 1.1 percent loss since the 2020 base.

Census figures put mean travel time to work at 26.8 minutes for county workers. Retail sales per capita reached $28,246 in 2022, which is high for a county of this size.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Mason County housing?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 numbers describe a modest-priced market where two of every three homes are owner-occupied and median household income is $52,178.

sections.h2: What are the Mason County tax collection dates and penalties?
sections.html:
The sheriff's Taxpayer's Notice lists four collection periods, and the bill arrives on a yellow postcard.

  • October 1 to November 1: 2% discount
  • November 2 to December 31: face amount
  • January: 5% penalty
  • February through April 15: 21% penalty

At the end of business on April 15, every unpaid real estate bill is transferred to the Mason County Clerk. From then on, according to the sheriff, payments are subject to a 20% County Attorney fee, a 10% County Clerk fee and interest at 1% per month, and the delinquency may be sold to a third party. Prior-year delinquent taxes are always paid at the clerk's office, and the sheriff gives 606-564-3341 for the amount due.

No past-due notices are mailed. Returned checks cost $50, and the bill reverts to unpaid status. Credit card payments are made through the online link, with an extra charge from the card company. If an escrow account or a new owner is responsible, the notice tells you to forward the bill immediately to that party. The statute behind the schedule is KRS 134.015.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Mason County assessment?
sections.html:
Talk to the PVA first. The City of Maysville's page on the Property Assessment Board of Appeals says the process is managed through the PVA, and that an owner who cannot reach a resolution there may appeal to the Board of Appeals. The City of Maysville has an appointee on the board, and the PVA's office, (606) 564-3700, is the contact the city lists.

The steps in KRS 133.120 are the same in every county. The conference must take place before or during the inspection period, and a petition to the clerk must follow within one workday after that period ends. The board then holds a hearing 25 to 35 days later under KRS 133.030.

  • Bring facts: comparable sales, a mortgage or appraisal document, insurance policies, or cost records.
  • A paid representative must be a professional listed in the statute, such as an attorney, accountant, tax consultant, licensed broker or appraiser.
  • Pay on your claimed value while the appeal runs.

Per the PVA's page, the office visits all property at least once every four years and may inspect and measure the outside of a building even if the owner is not home.

sections.h2: What is the Mason County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
The exemption removes $49,100 from the assessed value of a qualifying owner's home for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. The owner must be 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement-system program, and must live in the house.

Subtract it from the county's Census median home value of $161,500 and the taxable assessment is $112,400. Applications go to the PVA at 220 1/2 Sutton Street. The Mason County website says the PVA page also hosts the homestead or disability exemption application, along with property search and an affidavit for exoneration of vehicle property tax. Once accepted, an age-based claim stays in place while the same owner lives there, but a new owner has to apply.

sections.h2: How do I clear tax and record the deed when I sell in Mason County?
sections.html:
Call the sheriff for the current year's balance and the clerk for anything from earlier years, and settle both at closing. A lien for delinquent tax can last up to eleven years under KRS 134.015(5) regardless of who owns the parcel, so a title agent will insist on it.

The deed is recorded at the Mason County Clerk's office. The clerk collects the transfer tax of fifty cents for each $500 of value or fraction, a charge on the grantor set by KRS 142.050. At the county's median value of $161,500 that amounts to $161.50. The clerk's contact page lists four e-recording services, Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile and ePN, which title companies commonly use to submit documents electronically. Ask the clerk what each deed needs before you submit it.

faqs.q: Where is the Mason County Sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 120 West Third Street in Maysville, in the old Health Department building. Call 606-564-3309. Office hours are 9:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays.

faqs.q: What does a returned check cost in Mason County?
faqs.a: The sheriff charges $50, and the bill is set back to unpaid. Your repayment should then follow the payment period printed on the bill.

faqs.q: Does Mason County mail past-due notices?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff's notice says no past-due notices will be mailed, so watch the dates yourself. After April 15 unpaid real estate bills go to the County Clerk with added fees.

faqs.q: Who sets Mason County tax rates?
faqs.a: The fiscal court, city officials, school boards and other taxing authorities set them. The PVA does not set rates or decide the total to be raised.

faqs.q: Can I pay Mason County property tax by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes, through the online payment link on the sheriff's site. The card company adds its own charge. In person, by mail and the check-only drop box are the other options.
